problems.form_value: n_analyzed = 208 (Human-AI 72, Human-Human 136). Exclusions: 'The printed counts are the same at every stage ... The AUT mixed models use 139 groups (137 in the Human-Only models) of the 140 pairs, with no explanation (Tables 2 and 3).' Eligibility reason: 'the AUT models use 139 of the 140 pairs'.
problems.source_says: The 208/72/136 analyzed counts hold for Table 1 and the story diversity test only. They do not hold for the AUT mixed models, which carry the preregistered AUT originality and elaboration outcomes. The Human-Only model is the Covariates model with the AI responses removed (same covariates). The Base and Covariates models both have 2,970 observations, so all three models use the same 2,066 human responses, and these come from 137 pairs. The 2 extra groups in the Base and Covariates models hold only AI responses, so they are Human-AI pairs. So at least 3 of the 140 pairs (at least 2 of them Human-AI) give no human response to any AUT mixed model. These models analyze at most 205 people and at most 70 Human-AI participants. The paper prints no people count for them. The Levene tests, F(1, 3036) and F(1, 2132), use 3,038 and 2,134 responses, so the models also drop 68 human responses that the variance tests keep (904 AI responses in both). The paper does not explain either gap. The form's 'same at every stage' is therefore not right, and '139 of the 140 pairs' overstates the people in these models. Table 3 prints the same observation and group counts. Criterion 2 is not affected.

confirmed.statement: n_randomized = 208 (72 Human-AI, 136 Human-Human) matches the text as printed. The 208 Prolific recruits were randomly assigned to 72 Human-AI pairs (one person each) and 68 Human-Human pairs (two people each), and 72 + 136 = 208. The paper reports no unmatched partners, dropouts, or count before assignment.
confirmed.quote: Upon taking part in the study, participants were randomly assigned to either a human-AI (72 pairs) or human-human (68 pairs) condition.

confirmed.statement: Table 1 counts people: n = 208 (AI 72, Human 136). Race, gender, and education each sum to 208, 72, and 136, and the gender chi-square uses N = 208. This supports the form's arm split and counts_are = people.

confirmed.statement: Criterion 2 holds by a wide margin under any reading. The story diversity test covers 208 people in 140 pairs. Even the most restricted AUT model draws human responses from 137 pairs, so at least 137 people. Both arms also exceed the 65 pairs per group of the power analysis.

summary: Criterion 2 holds by a wide margin: 208 Prolific participants (72 with a GPT-4o partner, 136 in 68 human pairs) were randomly assigned and appear in Table 1, and the story diversity test uses all 140 pairs (pp. 4, 7, 15). The coding is refuted on one detail: the AUT mixed models in Tables 2 and 3 draw human responses from only 137 of the 140 pairs, so they analyze at most 205 people and at most 70 Human-AI participants, while the form records 208 analyzed (72 and 136) and describes those models as using 139 of 140 pairs.
